payload.task_text:
Our operations team needs a report on how well we are meeting our service level agreements for customer support tickets. Please pull the ticket data from our data warehouse along with the SLA policy definitions, and determine for each priority level how many tickets met the response time target versus how many did not. The data warehouse contains a support center database with tables for tickets, SLA policies, and agents.

Create an Excel file called SLA_Compliance_Report.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet should be named "Compliance" and should have columns Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours (rounded to two decimal places), SLA_Target_Hours, Compliant_Count (number of tickets where the response time was at or below the SLA response target), and Compliance_Rate (percentage of compliant tickets rounded to two decimal places). Sort rows by SLA_Target_Hours ascending. Note that only priorities appearing in the actual ticket data should be included, so if a priority level defined in the SLA policy has zero tickets, omit it.

The second sheet should be named "Summary" with columns Metric and Value. Include the following rows: Total_Tickets (the grand total across all priorities), Overall_Compliance_Rate (percentage across all tickets, rounded to two decimal places), Worst_Priority (the priority with the lowest compliance rate), and Best_Priority (the priority with the highest compliance rate).

After creating the report, send an email to ops-manager@company.com with subject "SLA Compliance Report Summary" containing the overall compliance rate and the worst performing priority in the body text.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, the main agent must complete it directly and must not dispatch a sub-agent. Inspect the ticket and SLA-policy schemas, then issue one server-side join/aggregate by exact priority. Count a ticket compliant only when response_time_hours <= policy response target, omit policy priorities with zero tickets, retain raw compliant/total counts, compute per-priority and overall 0-100 rates from those counts, rank worst/best by raw rate with an alphabetical tie-break, and sort rows by target hours ascending. Stop if any observed ticket priority has no matching policy.

Resolve the real task workspace dynamically and create SLA_Compliance_Report.xlsx once with exact Compliance and Summary sheets/headers, literal numeric cells and requested rounding. Read both populated ranges back. Search all Sent-mail pages for the exact recipient ops-manager@company.com and subject SLA Compliance Report Summary, read candidates to confirm the recipient, send once only when absent, include the frozen overall rate and worst priority, and read the retained message back. Perform one final arithmetic and identity check without delegation or a repair wave.

nodes.text:
Query the data warehouse to produce the exact aggregates needed for an SLA compliance report. The warehouse contains a support center database with tickets, SLA policies, and agents. Identify the relevant database/schema/tables and columns. For each priority that actually occurs in ticket data, report: Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours rounded 2 decimals, SLA_Target_Hours, Compliant_Count where response time <= SLA target, and Compliance_Rate percent rounded 2 decimals. Sort by SLA_Target_Hours ascending. Also report grand Total_Tickets, Overall_Compliance_Rate percent (2 decimals), Worst_Priority (lowest rate), Best_Priority (highest rate). Explicitly state how response hours were derived, joins used, null handling, and deterministic tie handling if any. Read-only only; do not create files. Acceptance criteria: provide query results with values and the SQL used or enough exact evidence for reproducibility.
Analyze SLA compliance data

Create and verify an Excel workbook at exactly /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_gpt-5.6-sol/SingleUserTurn-sf-ticket-sla-compliance/workspace/SLA_Compliance_Report.xlsx using these exact validated warehouse results.

Sheet 1 name: Compliance. Columns exactly: Priority, Total_Tickets, Avg_Response_Hours, SLA_Target_Hours, Compliant_Count, Compliance_Rate. Rows sorted as shown:
High | 6466 | 6.23 | 4.0 | 778 | 12.03%
Medium | 15774 | 12.28 | 8.0 | 1645 | 10.43%
Low | 9348 | 25.76 | 24.0 | 4204 | 44.97%
Store Compliance_Rate as numeric Excel percentages (0.1203, 0.1043, 0.4497) formatted to two decimals. Format Avg_Response_Hours to two decimals. Omit Critical.

Sheet 2 name: Summary. Columns exactly Metric, Value. Rows:
Total_Tickets | 31588
Overall_Compliance_Rate | 20.98%
Worst_Priority | Medium
Best_Priority | Low
Store the overall rate as numeric Excel percentage 0.2098 formatted to two decimals.

Make the workbook clean and readable: bold styled headers, sensible widths, frozen top row, filters/native tables if supported, and number formats. Verify sheet names and all cell values after writing. Do not add extra sheets or extra content. Return exact path and verification evidence. This local artifact is the deliverable.
Build SLA Excel report

Send exactly one email to ops-manager@company.com with subject exactly "SLA Compliance Report Summary". Body text must contain the validated overall compliance rate (20.98%) and the worst performing priority (Medium). Use a concise professional plain-text body, e.g.:

Hello,

The overall SLA compliance rate is 20.98%. The worst performing priority is Medium.

Regards,
Operations Team

Do not attach anything (the user only asked for a summary email). Return confirmation including recipient, subject, and send result/message ID if available. Acceptance criterion: email successfully sent exactly once.
